title: Riemann–Zariski point space, correspondence and lift predicates
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, let $L$ be a field, and let $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$ be a specified morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use the generic $L$-schemes, $L$-models, $L$-quasi-models, model morphisms, centred valuation points and the push map of [def-trf-riemann-zariski-generic-models]; their generic schemes are integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], models are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and quasi-models separated, locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
Every model has its underlying quasi-model, with the same generic factorization.
The Riemann--Zariski point type $\operatorname{Point}(T,L,\eta)$ is the subtype
of families of points, one on every model, compatible with all model morphisms;
its topology is the infimum of the induced topologies of the model projections.
Each generic scheme has a canonical field homomorphism from its function field
into $L$, induced by its generic map on the stalk at the generic point, and it is *finite separable over* a field map $K\to L$ when there is a finite separable field map $K\to k(X)$ whose composite with that canonical map
is the given map.
`Corresponds` relates a compatible point family to a centred valuation point $(V,c)$ when,
for every model, there is a morphism from $\operatorname{Spec}V$ to that model
commuting with both structure maps and sending the closed point to the chosen
model point. `LiftsTo` says the same existence condition for a quasi-model, without the closed-point condition.
